\[
R_\sigma(x) = -\sigma^2\, \nabla^2 (G_\sigma * I)(x),
\qquad
(x, \sigma) \text{ is a blob if } R_\sigma(x) = \max_{3 \times 3 \times 3} R \ge T,
\qquad
r = \sqrt{2}\, \sigma,\quad T = 0.2
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I\): The luma from 0 to 1, or 1 minus it for dark blobs
- \(G_\sigma\): A Gaussian of sigma
- \(\nabla^2\): The Laplacian, the sum of the second derivatives
- \(r\): The radius of the blob
- \(T\): The threshold

The Laplacian of a Gaussian blur is strongly negative in the middle of a bright blob whose size matches the blur. Its size shrinks as sigma grows, so it is multiplied by sigma^2 to make the scales comparable, the scale normalization of Lindeberg. The response R then has a peak at the center of each blob, at the scale that matches its size. For a disk of radius r, that scale is about sigma = r / sqrt(2). Here scikit-image builds R at evenly spaced scales. It keeps the points that are the largest of their 3 x 3 x 3 neighbors in position and scale and reach the threshold. Then it prunes blobs that overlap too much. The score is R at the peak.
